indicators.note: about here means turned around or rearranged, so the letters of note are shuffled

parts.note: 9-across is a doctor, and MB (Bachelor of Medicine) is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Someone is silenced over a message left by the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges NOTE into ENTO; the cross-reference to 9 (a doctor) gives MB, a medical degree.
explanation.definitionFit: To entomb someone is to shut them up inside a tomb, enclosing them completely.

explanation.surface: A police officer and a bloom set side by side.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper is British slang for a police officer, and so is bluebottle, from the blue uniform; the bluebottle is also the cornflower.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are names: old slang for a policeman, and a country name for the blue cornflower.

clue.text: Parting from soldier we encountered in autumn

indicators.note: in places the soldier and we inside the season word

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn
RE is the Royal Engineers, standing for a soldier
taken as written

explanation.surface: Saying goodbye to a soldier met in the autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: A farewell is a parting, the act of taking leave of someone.

explanation.surface: Something arriving as the year turns.
explanation.walkthrough: Advent means an arrival, and it is also the church season before Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is an arrival or coming; the other is the liturgical period leading to Christmas.

clue.text: Car for politician from the hearing

parts.note: Audi is a German make of car
a Tory is a member of the British Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A vehicle provided for a politician after a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing' looks like a court session, but it is the sense of hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Auditory describes what relates to or comes from the sense of hearing.

explanation.surface: Taking a carriage to the railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: A victoria is a light horse-drawn carriage; Victoria is also a major London railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an old four-wheeled carriage and a London terminus.

clue.text: Worker first gets requests to be agreeable

indicators.note: the worker comes after what is placed first, the requests

parts.note: pleas are earnest requests
the ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: An employee whose requests are granted first is happy to cooperate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worker' looks like the person making demands, but it is the ant, which follows PLEAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasant and agreeable are synonyms for something nice to deal with.

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A woman became his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue points to the first man, whom a girl (Eve) married.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the first man was given Eve as his wife, so a girl married him.

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning
taken as written

explanation.surface: An argument arises over something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns RE and IT together, giving TIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a row or level, as of seats in a theatre.

explanation.surface: Interfering with a skeleton.
explanation.walkthrough: To doctor something is to tamper with it; Bones (from sawbones) is slang for a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctoring means falsifying, and bones is old nickname slang for a medical man.

explanation.surface: Passing something to a diplomat.
explanation.walkthrough: To delegate is to hand over a task; a delegate is a representative, like an ambassador.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means entrust to another; the noun is a person sent to represent others.

clue.text: Don't annoy everybody by being vexatious

parts.note: annoy only part of the group: bother some people rather than all of them
annoy only part of the group: bother some people rather than all of them

explanation.surface: Advice not to irritate everyone, given by someone who is irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, not annoying everybody means you trouble only some.
explanation.definitionFit: Something troublesome causes bother or vexation, which is what vexatious means.

clue.text: Initiative and daring required for this undertaking

explanation.surface: Boldness is needed for this venture.
explanation.walkthrough: Enterprise means boldness and initiative, and also a project or venture.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a spirit of bold initiative and a business venture or project.

explanation.surface: Jeering at the soldiers' living quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: To barrack is British for jeering at someone, as a crowd does at sport.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means heckles, and the noun names buildings where soldiers live.

indicators.note: composition means putting together, here making a new arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Someone checked that a piece of writing was taken at a steady pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' looks like a piece of music, but it rearranges MADE SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Measured movement is slow and deliberate, which means unhurried.

clue.text: Point in hire charge for clothing

indicators.note: in puts the point inside the hire charge

parts.note: rent is the charge for hiring something
to aim is to point

explanation.surface: Something about the cost of renting outfits.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old literary word for clothing or garments.

indicators.note: reportedly means as said aloud, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: in rapture means in a trance

explanation.surface: Someone arrives in a state of delight, it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: IN TRANCE said aloud sounds like the word for an arrival on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor's entrance is the act of coming on stage.

parts.note: read as cultivation of the soil, split as until plus a long period of time

explanation.surface: A remark on staying married for many years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'husbandry' suggests marriage but means farming; the word splits as TILL (until) and AGE (a long time).
explanation.definitionFit: Tillage is the cultivation of land, a branch of husbandry in its farming sense.

clue.text: Bid to establish more than two centres

explanation.surface: An attempt to set up several hubs.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, three hearts is a bid; the heart is the centre of something, so three of them are more than two centres.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge call naming three tricks in hearts, and literally a trio of central cores.

clue.text: Mixed 10 losing, for example, in high spirits

indicators.note: mixed means the remaining letters are jumbled
losing means the letters for the example are taken away

parts.note: 10-across is a delegate

explanation.surface: A confused representative loses a sample but stays cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' removes EG from DELEGATE, leaving DELATE; 'Mixed' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: Elated means joyful and exhilarated, that is in high spirits.

explanation.surface: A woman who flopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' is a female, Miss as a title; a miss is a shot that does not hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss is the title for an unmarried woman, and a miss is a failed shot.

indicators.note: in places died inside the soldier

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
ob. (obiit) is the abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: A soldier perished in the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gobi is a large desert in Mongolia and China.

clue.text: Excessive devotion responsible for an attempt on revered figure

indicators.note: on means the attempt is placed after the revered figure

parts.note: an idol is a revered figure
an gives the article A
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A fan's obsession is to blame for an attack on a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Idolatry is extravagant worship or devotion to a person or thing.

clue.text: Old military role assumed by 9, perhaps

explanation.surface: A soldier's part taken on by the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: A lancer was a cavalry soldier with a lance; a doctor (9) lances boils, so is a lancer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancer names an old cavalry soldier and, humorously, one who lances, like a doctor.

clue.text: Baggage involved in double legal proceedings

parts.note: two words for legal proceedings: a suit and a case
two words for legal proceedings: a suit and a case

explanation.surface: Luggage caught up in two court actions.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitcase is an item of luggage, so belongs to one's baggage.

parts.note: T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia
as means when

explanation.surface: Lawrence was annoyed at being an editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Teased means annoyed or provoked with mockery, a form of irritation.
